skill_traces.query:
Sam: Hey Evan, some big news: I'm on a diet and living healthier! Been tough, but I'm determined.
Evan: Wow, Sam, that's great news! Making changes to live healthier can be challenging, how has it been going?
Sam: It's tough, but I'm sticking with it.
Evan: Nice work, Sam! Proud of you sticking to it. Have you noticed any positive changes?
Sam: Yes, there are many, such as more energy and less sluggishness after eating. This is really encouraging!
Evan: Wow, Sam, that's great to hear! Feeling more energized after meals is such a positive change. Keep up the good work! And speaking of healthy meals, do you have any favorite recipes you'd like to share?
Sam: Sure, I'm loving this recipe I found. It's a flavorful and healthy grilled chicken and veggie stir-fry. Wanna give it a go?
Evan: Mmm, looks yummy! Is the sauce a family secret? I'm always down to try new recipes!
Sam: Nah, it's just my homemade sauce. Want the recipe?
Evan: Yeah, I'd love to! Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Sam: Sure thing! Here's the recipe. Let me know how it went!
Evan: Thanks Sam! I'll give it a shot and let you know how it went. Trying out new recipes is a great way to stay busy and creative. By the way, I also started taking a painting classes few days ago and I'm really enjoying it. It's all about trying new things, right?
Sam: You're already good at drawing, why did you decide to join a class? And why did you start painting then years ago anyway?
Evan: Thanks, Sam! It all started when a friend of mine gave me this painting one day, it inspired me a lot and that's when I started painting. And I joined the classes to find like-minded people and show them what I can do, you can always improve your skills.
Sam: Wow, that's awesome! You're really talented. Did you take any other classes?
Evan: Thanks, Sam! Just been painting with these for now, but might look into other classes. It's awesome for finding my peace and expressing myself!
Sam: Cool, Evan! What have you been learning in those classes?
Evan: In painting classes, we've been learning about watercolors. The instructor stresses observing nature and painting what we see. It's a relaxing way to take a break from everyday stress.
Sam: Wow, Evan! What type of nature do you enjoy painting the most?
Evan: I love painting landscapes. Nature's beauty captivates me and brings me peace. Here's one of my recent works.
Sam: Wow, Evan! The colors are so bright. How do you capture the tranquil beauty of nature in your paintings?
Evan: Thanks Sam! I aim to capture the vibe of nature in my paintings, conveying the peacefulness of being outdoors.
Sam: Wow, that pic is great! Do you often spend time in places like this?
Evan: Thanks! I love being in places like this - it brings back memories of road tripping in my trusty car.
Sam: Wow, that's cool! Have you been to any fun places in that ride?
Evan: Yep, last month I drove somewhere fun. The views were amazing!
Sam: Did you take advantage of the skiing opportunities in Banff? Sounds like it would have been a lot of fun!
Evan: Yeah, it was great for skiing! The snow was amazing and I had a lot of fun. Can't wait to go back next year! Did you try any winter sports, Sam?
Sam: Ooh, skiing looks like a blast! I'd love to try it but I'm not sure my body can take it. What about you? What winter activities do you enjoy?
Evan: Skiing, snowboarding, and ice skating are all fun winter activities I enjoy.
Sam: Wish I could join in on the fun! It sounds awesome.
Evan: I'd like you to join me, too. Winter activities are a blast - hopefully someday you will!
Sam: Yeah, maybe. It's hard with that, you know. But who knows? Thanks for the understanding, Evan - it really means a lot.

selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.
selected.rerank_reason: Sam explicitly mentions sharing a photo of their recent painting, which triggers the photo-sharing event extraction.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user mentions what inspired or motivated their current or future project.
content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Attribute Memories to Actual Speaker
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting profile or preference memories from multi-party conversations, attribute each statement to the speaker who uttered it, not to another mentioned participant.
content: During extraction, treat each speaker's message as its own evidence unit: create a separate candidate per message and per speaker, and set the memory's subject to the speaker who uttered that message.
Do not merge opinions from different speakers into a single memory unless the speakers explicitly state the view jointly (e.g., 'we both like').
When a message contains a self-disclosure (e.g., 'I also have...', 'Yes, I...'), create a separate candidate for that speaker even if the message also contains a question or reply.
If the message text clearly attributes the preference to someone else (e.g., 'Tim loves...'), use that person only then; otherwise default to the speaker.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.
